findings.summary: The JSDoc says maxLength never splits a word, but when the first word is longer than maxLength the code truncates that word mid-word.
findings.detail: The doc comment says `maxLength` "caps the result, cutting at a separator so no word is split". The fallback `return slug.split(separator)[0].slice(0, maxLength);` (src/index.js:32) cuts the first word when it alone exceeds maxLength. The test 'cuts a first word that is longer than maxLength' depends on this: `"Supercalifragilistic expialidocious"` with maxLength 5 gives "super". Callers who trust the doc would not expect partial words. The behavior is reasonable and tested, so fix the doc rather than the code. Change the line to: "`maxLength` caps the result, cutting at the last separator that fits; if the first word alone is longer than `maxLength`, that word is truncated."
